meta.title: Reading and influences
meta.note: The order of these links changes from time to time. That is intentional. Learning is rarely linear, and neither is change.

tiers.label: Start here
tiers.microCopy: A way in, not a conclusion.

items.name: Nesta
items.annotation: Serious work on innovation for public good, systems change, and the limits of purely technical solutions.

items.name: Government Digital Service – Service Manual
items.annotation: Clear, practical guidance rooted in real delivery inside constrained public systems.

items.name: Institute for Government
items.annotation: Evidence-led analysis of how government actually works, including incentives, trade-offs, and institutional reality.

items.name: Behavioural Scientist
items.annotation: Accessible, thoughtful writing on behavioural science, decision-making, and the limits of rational models.

tiers.label: Go deeper
tiers.microCopy: When the simple explanations stop working.

items.name: Oxford Review (selected open articles)
items.annotation: Evidence-based management writing that challenges intuition, hype, and fashionable shortcuts.

items.name: Sensemaking by Dave Snowden
items.annotation: Cynefin, complexity, and decision-making under uncertainty, written from lived practice rather than theory alone.

items.name: Ribbonfarm
items.annotation: Long-form essays on organisations, power, technology, and modern work that resist simplification.

items.name: Aeon Essays
items.annotation: Carefully edited long-form essays that explore philosophy, culture, systems, and human behaviour.

tiers.label: Challenge your assumptions
tiers.microCopy: This may change how you see the problem.

items.name: Santa Fe Institute – Complexity Explorer Essays
items.annotation: Complexity as a discipline rather than a metaphor, with open material on emergence and adaptive systems.

items.name: AI Now Institute – Research & Writing
items.annotation: Critical work on AI, power, governance, and social impact that resists techno-neutral narratives.

items.name: The Maintainers
items.annotation: A corrective to innovation worship, focused on maintenance, care, and what keeps systems working.

items.name: Tyranny of Metrics (excerpted essays and talks)
items.annotation: Challenges measurement-driven management and the unintended consequences of performance obsession.

items.name: Ursula K. Le Guin – The Carrier Bag Theory of Fiction
items.annotation: A powerful reframing of progress, stories, and what we choose to value.

items.name: George Orwell – Politics and the English Language
items.annotation: A reminder that sloppy language enables sloppy thinking, especially in institutions.

items.name: John Berger – Ways of Seeing (excerpts)
items.annotation: On perception, power, and how framing shapes understanding.

items.name: Adam Curtis – Documentary essays (BBC)
items.annotation: Provocative narrative explorations of power, ideology, and unintended consequences.
